Fix $d\in\{2,5,8\}$ and put
$$SU(d)=\{T\in M_d(\mathbb C):T^*T=I_d,\ \det T=1\}.$$
A **certified $SU(d)$ matrix input** is an exact target $T\in SU(d)$ together
with a deterministic Cauchy-name procedure which, on unary input $1^b$ for
$b\ge1$, returns a rational complex matrix $Q_b$ such that each real and
imaginary coordinate of each entry differs from the corresponding coordinate
of $T$ by at most $2^{-b}$. The interface also specifies a worst-case bit-time
bound $t(b)$ for the query. A **polynomial-time name** has
$t(b)\le(b+1)^c$ for some fixed integer $c\ge1$. The target is the matrix
specified by the entire Cauchy name; if two targets satisfy these bounds for the same sequence $(Q_b)_{b\ge1}$,
every coordinate difference is at most $2^{1-b}$ for all $b$, hence is zero.
No individual $Q_b$ is required to be unitary or special unitary. A requested tolerance is a positive binary
rational and its numerator/denominator encoding length is recorded
separately. For $d=2$ this specializes the unary-name convention of
[[def-qc-effective-unitary-matrix-input]]. For $d=5,8$ it is the same
entrywise interface in the fixed block dimensions; no dimension is input to
an algorithm as an unbounded parameter.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

Use the Fibonacci fusion rule $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$ and the
fixed-chirality data
$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_\tau=\begin{pmatrix}\phi^{-1}&\phi^{-1/2}\\
\phi^{-1/2}&-\phi^{-1}\end{pmatrix}$ and
$r=R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$. The fixed-total-charge B6 path bases are

$$\mathcal P_1=\{0101010,0101110,0110110,0111010,0111110\},$$

$$\mathcal P_\tau=\{0101011,0101101,0101111,0110101,0110111,0111011,0111101,0111111\},$$

where each path is $(x_0,\ldots,x_6)$, $x_0=0$ is the unit label,
$x_1=1$ is $\tau$, and adjacent labels obey the fusion rule. For
$d_0=1,d_1=\phi$, define $E_i$ on either path basis by
$$(E_i)_{x,y}= \begin{cases} \sqrt{d_{x_i}d_{y_i}}/d_{x_{i-1}}, &x_j=y_j\ (j\ne i),\ x_{i-1}=x_{i+1}=y_{i-1}=y_{i+1},\\ 0,&\text{otherwise,} \end{cases} \qquad P_i:=\phi^{-1}E_i.$$
Then $P_i$ are orthogonal projections, have ranks $2$ on $\mathcal P_1$
and $3$ on $\mathcal P_\tau$, satisfy
$P_iP_{i+1}P_i=\phi^{-2}P_i$ and commute at separation at least two.
Consequently $B_i=rI+(1-r)P_i$ are unitary matrices satisfying the Artin
relations of $B_6$, with
$\det B_i=r^3$ on $V(\tau^6\to1)$ and $\det B_i=r^5$ on
$V(\tau^6\to\tau)$.

Let $\mathbb F$ be $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, let $A\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb F)$, and
let $\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge\sigma_r>0$ be the positive singular values of
$A$, where $r=\operatorname{rank}A$; write $\sigma_1=0$ when $r=0$.

1. **Spectral formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_2=\sigma_1$, where $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is
   the operator norm of [[def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space]].
2. **Frobenius formula.** $\lVert A\rVert_F=\bigl(\sigma_1^{2}+\cdots+\sigma_r^{2}\bigr)^{1/2}$.
3. **Unitary invariance.** For every unitary $U\in M_m(\mathbb F)$ and
   $V\in M_n(\mathbb F)$ (over $\mathbb F=\mathbb R$: orthogonal matrices),
   $$\lVert UAV\rVert_2=\lVert A\rVert_2,\qquad \lVert UAV\rVert_F=\lVert A\rVert_F.$$
4. **Sharp rank comparison.**
   $$\lVert A\rVert_2\;\le\;\lVert A\rVert_F\;\le\;\sqrt{r}\,\lVert A\rVert_2.$$
   The lower inequality is an equality exactly when $r\le 1$; the upper
   inequality is an equality exactly when $\sigma_1=\cdots=\sigma_r$, that is,
   when all nonzero singular values coincide. In particular
   $\lVert A\rVert_F\le\sqrt{\min(m,n)}\,\lVert A\rVert_2$.

$\mathcal O_X$-modules ([[def-module-on-ringed-space]]). Recall that for a

$\widetilde M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the sheaf of
$\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$-modules whose sections on a distinguished
open $D(f)$ are $M_f$
([[def-associated-sheaf-module-affine-scheme]]).

affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ and an $A$-module
$M$ such that

$$\mathcal F|_U\;\cong\;\widetilde M$$

as sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. A quasi-coherent sheaf of
$\mathcal O_X$-modules is also called a quasi-coherent module on $X$, and the
full subcategory of $\mathcal O_X$-modules consisting of the quasi-coherent
ones is written $\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$; morphisms in
$\operatorname{QCoh}(X)$ are all $\mathcal O_X$-module morphisms between its
objects.

Immediate consequences of the definition, used without further comment:

- The condition is invariant under isomorphism: if $\mathcal F\cong\mathcal G$
  as $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent, then so is
  $\mathcal G$, because the isomorphism restricts over an affine open.
- The condition is local on $X$: $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent if and only if
  there is an open cover $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ such that each restriction
  $\mathcal F|_{U_i}$ is quasi-coherent. Indeed a point of an arbitrary open
  subscheme $U\subseteq X$ has an affine open neighbourhood inside $U$, and an
  affine open subscheme of $X$ contained in $U$ is also an affine open
  subscheme of $U$; conversely, every point of $U_i$ lies in an affine open of
  $X$ inside $U_i$.
- If $\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent and $V\subseteq X$ is open, then
  $\mathcal F|_V$ is quasi-coherent, since $\mathcal F|_V$ is again an
  $\mathcal O_V$-module and an affine open $U\subseteq V$ is an affine open of
  $X$.

  point for an affine open neighbourhood on which $\mathcal F$ is associated to
  a module; it does not ask that $\mathcal F$ itself be associated to a single
  $A$-module. The affine comparison theorem on this page shows that on an
  affine scheme the two conditions coincide.

affine-module condition, and no finiteness, Noetherian or separatedness
hypothesis is part of it.
